textbookText: Let us take the case that we are measuring the diameter of a ball that is found as 2.64cm. Here, the digits 2 and 6 are reliable and certain while the last digit '4' is uncertain. Hence the diameter of the ball has a total 3 significant figures.

Let the measurement for the length of a rod be 3.5 cm. It has a total of 2 significant figures with 3 as reliable (certain) and the last digit 5 as uncertain. If we find the length as 3.56cm with some other device, it will be more precise and of more significant figures than 3.5cm. If the length of the same rod is measured as 3.567 cm using a micrometer screw gauge, it is more accurate than the former two.
Here are some rules to find the number of significant figures: i) All the non –zero digits in a given measurement are significant. i.e. 21.48 has total 4 significant figures Physics, Grade 11 | 9

ii) All the zeros between two non –zero digits are significant but leading zeros are not significant. i.e. 15.0041→ 6 significant figures. 2001 → 4 significant figures. 0015 → 2 significant figures iii) The zeros to the right of the last non-zero digit are not significant. i.e. 9800 → 2 significant figures. i.e. 050600 → 3 significant figures. iv)The zeros to the right of the decimal point and before (to the left of) the first non–zero digits are not significan .They only represent the position of the decimal point. i.e, 0.006 → 1 significant figure. 0.00025 → 2 significant figures. 0.0080038 → 5 significant figures. 0.25 → 2 significant figures. v) The zeros to right of the decimal number are significant only when there is a non-zero digit on its left 5.00→ 3 significant figure 5.0→ 2 significant figures 0.200→ 3 significant figures vi) In a measurement expressed in scientific notation, such as N× 10A, the 10A does not follow the rule of significant figures. 1.6 ×10-19 C → 2 significant figures 6.62 ×10-34 Js → 3 significant figures Physics, Grade 11 | 10

The rounding off of the significant figures is to omit one or more digits from the right side of the number until we attain the number of significant figures we want to round it off to. For the roundoff, look at the digit on the right end of the number. The rules for rounding off are as follows a) If the digit to be dropped out is less than 5, the preceding digit remains unchanged on rounding off. e.g. 123.42 ≈ 123.4 (in 4 significant numbers) ≈ 123 (in 3 significant number)
b) If the digit to be dropped out is greater than 5, the preceding digit is increased by 1 in rounding off. e.g. 123.167 ≈ 123.17 (in 5 significant numbers) ≈ 124.2 (in 4 significant numbers)
c) If the digit to be dropped out is exactly 5, the preceding digit to be retained is i) Increased by 1 if it is odd. eg. 12.35 ≈ 12.4 (in 3 significant numbers)
ii) kept unchanged if it is even. eg. 12.45 ≈ 12.4 (in 3 significant
numbers) 1.5.3 Significant Figures in mathematical operation
When two measurements are added or subtracted one from the other, the answer should
have the lowest decimal place as that of the input.

b) In Multiplication and Division: When two measurements are multiplied or divided one by other, the answer should have the lowest significant figures as that of the input. e.g. 118.6 ×16.2 = 1921.32 (Incorrect)

The concept of dimension of physical quantities was introduced in 1822 by Joseph Fourier.

The dimensions of a physical quantity are the powers that are raised to the fundamental quantities involved in a physical quantity. In mechanics; mass, length, and time are the three fundamental quantities represented respectively as [M], [L], and [T] in dimensional purpose. Temperature is represented
by [K], electric current is denoted by [A] or [I], and the amount of substance by [N] or [mol] . Likewise, the dimensional notation for the luminous intensity is [J] or [cd].
